messages:
nina: Quick signal: noticed a pattern of slow responses on /v1/embeddings when clients send 1000x tiny vectors vs 1x big vector. Routing shows requests landing on cold shard fastpath and getting serialized.

tom: Is this the same tenant that hit the preflight 'bytes per request' softcap? If so, splitter might be re-chunking and creating many small frames which kills RPC fanout.

ravi: I pulled traces: client sends 1k frames of 64-dim vectors, header X-Embed-Dims=64, content-length ~80kb. Preflight currently computes units as max(dims*frames, bytes/16) => it's treating per-dim heavily. For very high frame counts, the unit calculation pushes it into slowpath.

laura: That formula was intentional to prevent small high-dim blasts from gaming quotas, but we didn't anticipate many small vectors with low dims. Should quota be additive (frames + dims) not multiplicative?

nina: Two user stories: (A) embeddings-as-rows use-case (many short vectors) expects low latency; (B) single-document chunking use-case expects throughput. We need different routing/units for each.

tom: Proposal: introduce a dual-unit model: `embed.units = max(bytes_based_units, dims_based_units)` but also tag requests with `ingress.hint=rows|chunks`. If hint=rows, prefer fastpath that optimizes RPC coalescing and increases per-tenant concurrency. If hint=chunks, keep current conservative units.

ravi: How do we get clients to set hint? SDKs can set it automatically based on request shape (#frames > 50 -> rows). Also allow server-side heuristics for unlabeled traffic.

laura: Console UX: add a toggle per-tenant "treat embeddings as rows (low-latency)" with warning about possible higher cost if the tenant sends large dims. Also show a small simulation panel that estimates units/cost for sample payload.

nina: Telemetry: add metric `embed.ingress.shape_hint{hint=rows|chunks|auto}` and `embed.ingress.coalesced_rpc_latency_ms` to measure fastpath effectiveness. Also track `embed.units_estimate` histogram.

tom: Routing changes: fastpath shard requires the splitter to batch many small frames into a single RPC where possible. We'll need to implement local coalescing in the ingress node and an RPC protocol tweak to accept buffered frames. That could be an opt-in feature flag.

ravi: Safety: for opt-in fastpath ensure we keep per-tenant soft caps and a backpressure signal so one noisy tenant doesn't starve others. Suggest token-bucket per-tenant on ingress with dynamic refill based on observed latency.

laura: Rollout plan: (1) add hint header and SDK auto-detection behind FF, (2) implement ingress coalescer + fastpath proto on canary, (3) expose console toggle + simulation, (4) run for 4 weeks with telemetry dashboards.

nina: Action items: ravi will prototype ingress coalescer (PR), tom will update unit calc RFC, laura will mock console simulation, i'll add telemetry panels and an alert `embed.coalesced_rpc_latency_ms_p95 > 200ms` to fire.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: feature-flag "embed-fastpath-rows" enabled on canary (2% traffic).

ravi: I'll wire in a small sampling trace (1/1000) to validate coalescing correctness and to ensure no reorder issues. If we see errors, revert fastpath.

tom: Also update docs: /v1/embeddings API page should document `X-Embed-Shape-Hint` and include examples for rows vs chunks.

laura: One more UI thing: add a per-route "expected units" preview in the Console when you paste a sample payload so customers can tune dims vs frames before sending.

nina: Great. let's keep communication tight while canary runs. Post-mortem if we see regressions.
